claim: Amazon CloudWatch monitors your AWS resources and the applications you run on AWS in real time, and offers tools for system-wide observability of application performance, operational health and resource utilization.
question: What does Amazon CloudWatch do?

values.display: monitors your Amazon Web Services (AWS) resources

evidence.quote: Amazon CloudWatch monitors your Amazon Web Services (AWS) resources and the applications you run on AWS in real time, and offers many tools to give you system-wide observability of your application performance, operational health, and resource utilization.

claim: CloudWatch provides two types of metrics: OpenTelemetry Metrics, which the documentation marks as recommended, and CloudWatch Metrics (Classic).
question: What two types of metrics does CloudWatch provide?

evidence.quote: CloudWatch provides two types of metrics: OpenTelemetry Metrics (recommended) and CloudWatch Metrics (Classic).

claim: Many AWS services automatically report metrics into CloudWatch, and you can also publish your own custom metrics with OpenTelemetry (OTLP) or with the PutMetricData API.
question: How do metrics get into CloudWatch?

evidence.quote: Many AWS services automatically report metrics into CloudWatch, and you can also publish your own custom metrics, either with OpenTelemetry (OTLP) or with the PutMetricData API.

claim: CloudWatch provides curated automatic dashboards for many AWS services so that you do not have to build them yourself.
question: Do you have to build a dashboard for each AWS service by hand?

values.display: don't have to build them yourself

evidence.quote: CloudWatch provides curated automatic dashboards for many AWS services, so that you don't have to build them yourself.

claim: Many AWS services offer basic monitoring by publishing a default set of metrics to CloudWatch at no charge, and basic monitoring is enabled automatically when you start using such a service.
question: Is basic monitoring on by default and is it free?

evidence.quote: Many AWS services offer basic monitoring by publishing a default set of metrics to CloudWatch with no charge to customers. By default, when you start using one of these AWS services, basic monitoring is automatically enabled.

claim: Detailed monitoring is offered by only some services, it incurs charges, and you must choose to activate it for an AWS service.
question: Is detailed monitoring on by default and is it free?

values.display: you must choose to activate it

evidence.quote: Detailed monitoring is offered by only some services. It also incurs charges. To use it for an AWS service, you must choose to activate it.

claim: Amazon EC2 detailed monitoring publishes metrics at one-minute intervals, instead of the five-minute intervals used in EC2 basic monitoring.
question: How often does EC2 publish metrics with basic and with detailed monitoring?

evidence.quote: For example, Amazon EC2 detailed monitoring provides more frequent metrics, published at one-minute intervals, instead of the five-minute intervals used in Amazon EC2 basic monitoring.

claim: Detailed monitoring has different names in different services: detailed monitoring in Amazon EC2, enhanced monitoring in AWS Elastic Beanstalk, and request metrics in Amazon S3.
question: What is detailed monitoring called in Elastic Beanstalk and in Amazon S3?

evidence.quote: In different AWS services, detailed monitoring also has different names. For example, in Amazon EC2 it is called detailed monitoring, in AWS Elastic Beanstalk it is called enhanced monitoring, and in Amazon S3 it is called request metrics.

claim: Application Signals automatically detects and monitors an application's key performance indicators such as latency, error rates and request rates, without manual instrumentation or code changes.
question: Which CloudWatch feature gives application performance monitoring without code changes?

values.display: without manual instrumentation or code changes

evidence.quote: With Application Signals you can automatically detect and monitor your applications' key performance indicators like latency, error rates, and request rates without manual instrumentation or code changes.

claim: CloudWatch Synthetics runs configurable scripts called canaries that simulate user behavior to monitor your endpoints and APIs and alert you to availability issues or performance degradation before they affect real users.
question: Which CloudWatch feature checks endpoints on a schedule like a customer would?

evidence.quote: CloudWatch Synthetics complements this by enabling you to proactively monitor your endpoints and APIs through configurable scripts called *canaries* that simulate user behavior and alert you to availability issues or performance degradation before they impact real users.

claim: Canaries are configurable scripts that run on a schedule and follow the same routes and perform the same actions as a customer, so you can verify the customer experience even when you have no customer traffic.
question: Can a canary verify availability when there is no real traffic?

values.display: configurable scripts that run on a schedule
even when you don't have any customer traffic

evidence.quote: You can use Amazon CloudWatch Synthetics to create *canaries*, configurable scripts that run on a schedule, to monitor your endpoints and APIs. Canaries follow the same routes and perform the same actions as a customer, which makes it possible for you to continually verify your customer experience even when you don't have any customer traffic on your applications.

claim: CloudWatch RUM performs real user monitoring: it collects and shows client-side performance data of web and mobile applications from actual user sessions in near real time.
question: Which CloudWatch feature measures performance from real user sessions in the browser or app?

evidence.quote: With CloudWatch RUM, you can perform real user monitoring to collect and view client-side data about your web and mobile application performance from actual user sessions in near real time.

claim: Service Level Objectives (SLOs) in CloudWatch let you define, track and alert on specific reliability targets for your applications, using error budgets and SLO compliance over time.
question: How do you track a reliability target such as availability in CloudWatch?

evidence.quote: Use Service Level Objectives (SLOs) in CloudWatch to define, track, and alert on specific reliability targets for your applications, helping you maintain service quality commitments by setting error budgets and monitoring SLO compliance over time.

claim: Database Insights lets you monitor database performance metrics in real time, analyze SQL query performance and troubleshoot database load for AWS database services.
question: Which CloudWatch feature analyzes SQL query performance for AWS databases?

evidence.quote: Database Insights allows you to monitor database performance metrics in real time, analyze SQL query performance, and troubleshoot database load issues for AWS database services.

claim: Lambda Insights provides system-level metrics for Lambda functions, including memory and CPU utilization tracking and cold start detection and analysis.
question: Which CloudWatch feature shows memory and CPU use and cold starts for Lambda functions?

evidence.quote: Lambda Insights provides system-level metrics for Lambda functions, including memory and CPU utilization tracking, and cold start detection and analysis.

claim: Container Insights collects and analyzes metrics from containerized applications on Amazon ECS clusters, Amazon EKS clusters and self-managed Kubernetes clusters on Amazon EC2.
question: Which CloudWatch feature collects metrics from ECS and EKS containers?

values.display: Amazon ECS clusters, Amazon EKS clusters

evidence.quote: Container Insights allows you to collect and analyze metrics from containerized applications, on Amazon ECS clusters, Amazon EKS clusters, and self-managed Kubernetes clusters on Amazon EC2.

claim: Contributor Insights analyzes log data and creates time series of the top-N contributors, the total number of unique contributors and their usage, which helps you find top talkers such as bad hosts or the heaviest network users.
question: Which CloudWatch feature finds the top talkers in high-cardinality log data?

evidence.quote: You can use Contributor Insights to analyze log data and create time series that display contributor data. You can see metrics about the top-N contributors, the total number of unique contributors, and their usage. This helps you find top talkers and understand who or what is impacting system performance.

claim: Metric streams continually stream CloudWatch metrics to a destination of your choice with near-real-time delivery and low latency; with a custom setup you direct the stream to an Amazon Data Firehose delivery stream.
question: How can you send CloudWatch metrics to S3 or a third-party tool in near real time?

evidence.quote: You can use *metric streams* to continually stream CloudWatch metrics to a destination of your choice, with near-real-time delivery and low latency.
Custom setup with Firehose— Create a metric stream and direct it to an Amazon Data Firehose delivery stream that delivers your CloudWatch metrics to where you want them to go.

claim: Transaction Search is an interactive analytics experience that gives complete visibility of your application transaction spans, the fundamental units of operation in a distributed trace.
question: Which CloudWatch feature lets you search transaction spans?

evidence.quote: Transaction Search is an interactive analytics experience you can use to get complete visibility of your application transaction spans.

claim: CloudWatch includes automatic pre-built dashboards and lets you create your own; dashboards let you monitor resources in a single view, even resources spread across different Regions.
question: Can one CloudWatch dashboard show resources from several Regions?

evidence.quote: Amazon CloudWatch includes automatic pre-built dashboards and also enables you to create your own dashboards. Dashboards help you to monitor your resources in a single view, even those resources that are spread across different Regions.

claim: In a monitoring account with CloudWatch cross-account observability, a single dashboard graph can include metrics from multiple source accounts, and you can create alarms in the monitoring account that watch metrics in source accounts.
question: Can one dashboard graph combine metrics from different accounts?

values.display: Create alarms in the monitoring account

evidence.quote: Search, view, and create graphs of metrics that reside in source accounts. A single graph can include metrics from multiple accounts.
Create alarms in the monitoring account that watch metrics in source accounts.

claim: You can share a CloudWatch dashboard with people who do not have direct access to your account in three ways: with a few designated email addresses (each user creates a password), publicly with anyone who has the link, or with all dashboards through a SAML single sign-on provider integrated with Amazon Cognito.
question: How can you share a CloudWatch dashboard with people outside your account?

values.display: designate as many as five email addresses

evidence.quote: Share a single dashboard and designate as many as five email addresses of people who can view the dashboard. Each of these users creates their own password that they must enter to view the dashboard.
Share a single dashboard publicly, so that anyone who has the link can view the dashboard.
Share all the CloudWatch dashboards in your account and specify a third-party single sign-on (SSO) provider for dashboard access.

claim: To share all dashboards through a third-party single sign-on provider, you integrate the provider with Amazon Cognito and the provider must support SAML.
question: What does SSO-based dashboard sharing require?

values.display: integrate the SSO provider with Amazon Cognito
must support Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML)

evidence.quote: To enable this, you integrate the SSO provider with Amazon Cognito. The SSO provider must support Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML).

claim: Sharing a dashboard does not incur charges, but the widgets inside a shared dashboard incur charges at standard CloudWatch rates.
question: Does sharing a CloudWatch dashboard cost extra?

values.display: widgets inside a shared dashboard incur charges

evidence.quote: Sharing a dashboard doesn't incur charges, but widgets inside a shared dashboard incur charges at standard CloudWatch rates.

claim: Everyone you share a dashboard with is granted the sharing permissions, and because cloudwatch:GetMetricData and ec2:DescribeTags cannot be scoped down, they can query all CloudWatch metrics and the names and tags of all EC2 instances in the account.
question: What can people with access to a shared dashboard see beyond the dashboard?

values.display: names and tags of all EC2 instances

evidence.quote: The `cloudwatch:GetMetricData` and `ec2:DescribeTags` permissions cannot be scoped down to specific metrics or EC2 instances, so the people with access to the dashboard can query all CloudWatch metrics and the names and tags of all EC2 instances in the account.

claim: Billing metric data (estimated charges) is stored in the US East (N. Virginia) Region and represents worldwide charges, so you must set the Region to US East (N. Virginia) before you create a billing alarm.
question: In which Region do you create a CloudWatch billing alarm?

qualifiers.condition: Billing alerts must be enabled first.

evidence.quote: Billing metric data is stored in the US East (N. Virginia) Region and represents worldwide charges.
Before you create a billing alarm, you must set your Region to US East (N. Virginia).

claim: Before you can create an alarm for estimated charges you must enable billing alerts; after you enable them you cannot disable data collection, but you can delete the billing alarms you created.
question: What must you do before you can create a CloudWatch billing alarm?

evidence.quote: Before you can create an alarm for your estimated charges, you must enable billing alerts, so that you can monitor your estimated AWS charges and create an alarm using billing metric data. After you enable billing alerts, you can't disable data collection, but you can delete any billing alarms that you created.

claim: A billing alarm triggers only when the current billing exceeds the threshold you specify; it does not use projections based on your usage so far in the month.
question: Does a CloudWatch billing alarm use a forecast of month-end charges?

values.display: only when the current billing exceeds the threshold

evidence.quote: The alarm triggers when your account billing exceeds the threshold you specify. It triggers only when the current billing exceeds the threshold. It doesn't use projections based on your usage so far in the month.

claim: When you create a billing alarm you specify an Amazon SNS topic to be notified when the alarm is in the ALARM state; the topic can include your email address.
question: How does a billing alarm notify you?

evidence.quote: Then specify an Amazon SNS topic to be notified when your alarm is in the `ALARM` state. The Amazon SNS topic can include your email address so that you receive email when the billing amount crosses the threshold that you specified.

claim: In a consolidated billing account, member linked account metrics are captured only if the payer account enables the Receive Billing Alerts preference.
question: Who must turn on billing alerts for linked accounts in consolidated billing?

values.display: only if the payer account enables

evidence.quote: In a consolidated billing account, member linked account metrics are captured only if the payer account enables the **Receive Billing Alerts** preference.
